title: Effect of a structured simulator action
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $x,a,b$ be Boolean words, let $q,q'$ be simulator states, let $p$ be an input-head position for $x$, let $h_a,h_b$ be integers, and let $o$ be an output word. For movements $m_i,m_a,m_b\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and an optional output bit $e$, applying the action that moves the input head by $m_i$, makes no writes, moves the first two work heads by $m_a,m_b$, emits $e$, and enters $q'$ gives the configuration with state $q'$, input position moved by $m_i$, buffers $a,b$, head positions $h_a+m_a,h_b+m_b$, and output $o$ followed by $e$ when present.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$p$ is a valid input-head position for $x$
